method: Read-only complete runtime-diff/new-module/caller/test review using review-agent. Self-review by the implementing agent, not independent review.
resolvedDuringImplementation: Open axle bays in the old full-width floor to expose the actual suspension assemblies.
Report wheels released through control-arm failure in the existing applyImpact return contract.
Keep rear pipe impacts separate from the engine manifold and require the rear pipe for visible outlet mounting.
Include missing wheel mass alongside the separate structural assemblies.
limits: The full 156-requirement objective remains active. Next: Phase 4 interiors/cockpit/navigation/mirrors/driver; detailed engine bays and dismantling remain Phase 6.

Suspension and pipe geometry, damage thresholds and rigid proxies are authored browser approximations, not a full multibody/soft-body model. Underfloor abrasion uses the existing four-wheel sampled road plane.
Eight loose body/underbody assemblies share a pool. Debris stays local, with static-world contacts only. Older protocol-18 clients ignore added visual details.
Browser tests use local Chromium software rendering and public PeerJS/WebRTC. No physical-controller, subjective-listening or separate mobile/TURN acceptance. CPU samples are not FPS guarantees.
